title.en: Prepare the Profit and Loss Appropriation Account
Calculate interest on capital, salary and commission

say.en: A firm earns 2,10,000 rupees. Before partners split it in their ratio, the deed promises interest, salary and commission. In what order do we pay them? The Profit and Loss Appropriation Account shows exactly this. In this lesson: Prepare the Profit and Loss Appropriation Account.
Calculate interest on capital, salary and commission.
Handle insufficient profits.

body.en: The account starts with net profit from the Profit and Loss Account (credit side), plus interest on drawings. On the debit side come interest on capital, partners' salary and commission, and transfer to reserve. The balance is the divisible profit, shared in the profit sharing ratio. Interest on capital is an *appropriation*, not a charge, so it is allowed only out of profits.
body.kn: ವಿನಿಯೋಗ ಖಾತೆಯ ಜಮಾ ಬದಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ನಿವ್ವಳ ಲಾಭ ಮತ್ತು ಸೆಳೆತಗಳ ಮೇಲಿನ ಬಡ್ಡಿ; ಖರ್ಚು ಬದಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ಬಂಡವಾಳದ ಮೇಲಿನ ಬಡ್ಡಿ, ವೇತನ, ಕಮಿಷನ್, ಮೀಸಲು ವರ್ಗಾವಣೆ. ಉಳಿದ ಲಾಭವನ್ನು ಲಾಭ ಹಂಚಿಕೆ ಅನುಪಾತದಲ್ಲಿ ಹಂಚಲಾಗುತ್ತದೆ.

say.en: Let us work this out together, step by step. A and B share profits 3:2. Capitals: A 4,00,000, rupees B 3,00,000 rupees. Interest on capital 10 percent p.a.; B's salary 3,000 rupees per month; A's commission 10 percent of net profit before charging it. Net profit 2,10,000 rupees. Distribute the profit.
Interest on capital: A 40,000, rupees B 30,000 rupees. Salary to B: 3,000 times 12 equals 36,000 rupees.
Commission to A: 10 percent of 2,10,000 equals 21,000 rupees.
Total appropriations equals 40,000 plus 30,000 plus 36,000 plus 21,000 equals 1,27,000 rupees; divisible profit equals 2,10,000 minus 1,27,000 equals 83,000 rupees.
A: 83,000 times 3 over 5 equals 49,800 rupees; B: 83,000 times 2 over 5 equals 33,200 rupees.
So the answer is A gets 40,000 plus 21,000 plus 49,800 equals 1,10,800 rupees; B gets 30,000 plus 36,000 plus 33,200 equals 99,200 rupees (total 2,10,000 rupees).
